Package com.egradx.auth

Class EgradxUserService

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.EgradxUserService
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
public class EgradxUserService extends Object implements org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
Administering the users inside one organization: who's a member, adding someone with a role, changing their details or role, deactivating them.

This is deliberately separate from EgradxAuthService, which covers a user acting on their own behalf (register, log in, refresh, log out). Everything here is somebody administering other people, and every operation is scoped to an organization — there is no "list all users on the platform" call, because that isn't a question a tenant admin should be able to ask.

Note createUser(java.util.UUID, com.egradx.auth.dto.EgradxCreateOrganizationUserRequest) creates a user already attached to an organization with a role, unlike EgradxAuthService.register, which deliberately creates a user belonging to nothing.

      @Transactional public EgradxOrganizationUserDto createUser(UUID organizationId, EgradxCreateOrganizationUserRequest request)
      Creates a user and makes them a member of this organization with the named role, in one step.

    • updateUser

      @Transactional public EgradxOrganizationUserDto updateUser(UUID organizationId, UUID userId, EgradxUpdateOrganizationUserRequest request)
      Partial update — only the fields present on the request are touched; see EgradxUpdateOrganizationUserRequest.
      Throws:
      NotFoundException - if the user isn't a member of this organization, or the new role name doesn't exist in it
      DuplicateResourceException - if a new username/email is already taken by someone else

    • deactivateUser

      @Transactional public void deactivateUser(UUID organizationId, UUID userId, UUID actingUserId)
      Soft-deactivates the user (they keep their membership and role, but can no longer log in, and any live session is cut off on its very next request by EgradxPermissionResolver).
      Throws:
      ValidationException - if a user tries to deactivate themselves — the quickest way for an organization to lock itself out
